scenes.say: Async and await make C sharp code easier, but what’s the difference between Task and ValueTask?

scenes.label: Task
scenes.sub: Represents an async operation; always allocates.
scenes.say: Task is the standard for asynchronous operations. It always creates an object, even if the work finishes instantly.

scenes.label: ValueTask
scenes.sub: Lightweight; avoids allocation if done sync.
scenes.say: ValueTask is lighter. It skips allocation when the operation completes synchronously, like returning a cached value.
ConfigureAwait false tells await not to capture the context. This helps prevent deadlocks, especially in UI or ASP.NET code.

scenes.question: Is ConfigureAwait(false) a universal fix?
scenes.right: No. It avoids context capture, but deadlocks can still happen for other reasons.
scenes.say: ConfigureAwait false isn’t a magic bullet. It avoids context capture, but deadlocks can still occur for other reasons.
